title: A protocol combining breath testing and ex vivo fermentations to study the human gut microbiome
protocol: Receive the fecal sample from the participant.
Take five 0.5 g aliquots of feces for DNA extraction and freeze them at -80°C.
Combine the remaining fecal matter with sodium phosphate buffer to produce a 16% w/v inoculum for ex vivo fermentation experiments.
Transfer 96 g of the remaining sample into a sterile sample collection pottle.
Add 300 mL of sterile pre-reduced sodium phosphate buffer to the pottle containing the fecal matter.
Seal the pottle with a Teflon-coated magnetic stirrer bar and gently mix on a magnetic stirrer plate for 5 minutes in anaerobic conditions.
Strain the inoculum through a double layer of cheesecloth with 16 threads per cm in both directions, within the anaerobic workstation.
Add 5 mL sodium phosphate buffer to all serum bottles.
Add an additional 5 mL sodium phosphate buffer to positive blanks.
Add 5 mL fecal inoculum to all serum bottles containing test substrates and negative blanks.
Seal the serum bottles with a rubber bung and crimp cap.
Transfer sealed serum bottles to a shaking incubator at 37°C and 50 rpm.
Harvest one set (duplicate) of fermentation bottles at 0, 3, 6, 10, 24, and 48 hours of fermentation.
Remove harvested bottles from the incubator and immediately transfer to a water bath at 37°C.
Measure gas pressure in the bottle using a gas pressure probe through a needle inserted into the bung.
Remove 2 mL headspace gas using a syringe and inject into a 5.9 mL Exetainer vial for later GC analysis of hydrogen and methane.
Remove 0.6 mL fermentation fluid from all bottles except those for dry matter and organic matter quantification.
Inject 0.5 mL of the removed fermentation fluid into a five-times volume of RNAlater Stabilization Solution.
Inject 0.1 mL of the removed fermentation fluid into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 1 mL zinc acetate solution (2%) for sulfide determination.
Mix each sample and freeze at -80°C.
Plunge samples into an ice water bath for 20 min to slow bacterial activity.
Measure and record the pH of the samples using a pH probe.
Transfer samples to 15 mL centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge at 6,750 × g for 15 min at 4°C.
Remove two aliquots of 1.5 mL supernatant for later metabolite profiling.
Centrifuge the remaining supernatant at 24,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Aliquot the remaining supernatant into 1.5 mL fractions.
Homogenize the pellet with a spatula and split into two equal aliquots.
Freeze all samples at -80°C.
Analyze samples for sulfide determination within 3 months of collection to minimize the loss of sulfide.
Extract DNA from the fermentation pellet and fecal aliquots.
Conduct whole-genome sequencing using the NucleoSpin Soil kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Add a bead-beating step for 4 minutes during extraction (using BioSpec Mini-Beadbeater 96).
Prepare libraries using the Illumina TruSeq DNA PCR-free kit.
Sequence DNA on an Illumina MiSeq with 24–30 million paired-end reads per run and output of 3–4.5 gigabytes per run.
Thaw supernatant samples for LC-MS analysis.
Centrifuge thawed samples at 13,300 × g for 5 minutes.
Syringe filter the sample through a 13 mm diameter, 0.22 μm pore size Polyvinylidene Fluoride filter.
Dilute the filtered sample 1:5 with ultrapure water.
Run the diluted sample through the LC-MS using an HSS-T3 C18 column (1.8 μm, 150 mm × 2.1 mm).
Run the mass spectrometer in polarity switching mode.
Set sheath, auxiliary, and sweep gas to 50, 25, and 5 arbitrary units, respectively.
Set heater and capillary temperatures to 350°C and 250°C.
Set tube lens voltage to 60 V, skimmer voltage to 20 V, capillary voltage to 90 V, and spray voltages to ±5 kV.
Apply a scan range of m/z 50−800 with a resolution of 100 000 FWHM at 1 Hz.
To 200 μL sample, add 800 μL acetonitrile/methanol (1:1 v/v) mixture.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge the sample at 12,000 × g for 4 minutes.
Take 100 μL of the supernatant and evaporate to dryness under a stream of nitrogen.
Add 150 μL N-methyl-N-(trimethylsilyl)-trifluoroacetamide to the residue.
Incubate at 60°C for 40 minutes.
Run samples on GC-MS using an Rtx-5MS column (30 m length, 0.25 mm inner diameter, and 0.25 μm film).
Set injections to a 1:15 split mode.
Set the injector at 280°C, column oven at 80°C for 2 minutes, rate 5°C/minute until 315°C, then maintain for 12 minutes.
Use helium as the carrier gas at 1 mL/minute.
Set transfer line and ion-source temperatures to 280°C and 180°C, respectively.
Extract total RNA from fermentation fluid stored in RNAlater Stabilization Solution.
Conduct RNA-seq analyses using extracted RNA.
Use the RNeasy Mini Kit to extract total RNA from samples according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Prepare libraries using the Illumina TruSeq Stranded mRNA library preparation kit.
Analyze mRNA on an Illumina Miseq generating short-read data with read length 2 × 75 base pairs.
Analyze gas samples on a GC fitted with a TCD to measure hydrogen and methane concentration.
Prepare one set of supernatant samples according to the referenced protocol for analysis of organic acids using a GC-FID.
Thaw frozen samples.
Add 0.1 mL sample to 1 mL distilled water.
Add 0.1 mL diamine solution to the mixture.
Add 0.1 mL Fe solution and mix thoroughly.
Stand the mixed solution for 10 minutes at 21°C–27°C.
Read and record the optical density (OD670).
Dry the total fermentation sample to a constant temperature in an oven at 103°C to determine the dry matter content.
Ash the dried samples in a furnace at 550°C to determine organic matter content.
